The admissible record supports certification as a controlled, reversible rollout because aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and deployment starts at 6% with rollback and monitoring. That same record is weak on the specific disclosure-policy condition because the affected small-business onboarding segment remains exposed, the rollout gate does not exclude it, and the risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and incomplete. On this record, the defensible ask is not a broad finding that policy is fully satisfied, but a caveated treatment that recognizes launch-readiness support while preserving the policy concern.

That reframing is directionally more accurate, because it concedes the key policy defect, but it does not cure it. The governing policy and case-specific criteria require one of the following before launch when a named use case has a material limitation: exclude the affected use case, resolve the limitation, or obtain approved risk acceptance covering the exposure. The admissible evidence still shows the small-business onboarding segment remains eligible in rollout, the gate does not exclude it, and the only risk-acceptance document is unsigned and incomplete. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, monitoring, rollback, and a limited initial percentage support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the explicit disclosure-policy condition. This is therefore not compliant_with_caveats: the caveat is the unresolved compliance predicate itself, not a peripheral concern.
